correctness.rationale: The gradient of determinant along independent diagonals excludes all corank-one singularities. Nonzero cyclic offdiagonal entries force nullity at most two and adjacent evaluations of the kernel to be isomorphisms. The Pluecker three-term relation reconstructs a unique projective symmetric matrix from any two-plane with all adjacent Pluecker minors nonzero. The mutually inverse constructions are morphisms. On the corank-two stratum a Schur-complement chart has three transverse entries, and changing the two adjacent diagonals and their connecting edge spans Sym^2(K*), giving the completed ordinary-double-point equation and radical Jacobian ideal at every point. For k>=2 zero edges there are k path blocks and two independent nonconstant block-determinant equations are necessary for corank two, giving ambient codimension at least four. The attached 84 exact rational examples verify formulas but do not replace this general proof.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text historical study treats a narrower normalized periodic second-order recurrence: its Grassmannian image imposes equal consecutive Pluecker coordinates and has dimension n-3, whereas the claimed locus is the entire nonzero-consecutive-minors open in Gr(2,n), of dimension 2n-4. The published four-cycle-Grassmannian complement result describes U_4 and its topology but does not identify it with the singular locus of symmetric cyclic sparse determinant hypersurfaces or prove uniform transverse nodal germs. The own archive includes a distinct path-tridiagonal determinantal singularity result, but path closure gives different strata. No consulted source contains or strongly implies the combined reconstruction and local statement; unindexed equivalent periodic Jacobi/minimum rank literature remains a real residual risk.

value.rationale: The rank-two singular stratum of the determinant of a periodic Jacobi support is a natural infinite geometric family. Determining it as an explicitly reconstructed smooth affine Gr open, with pointwise rather than merely generic A1 transverse singularities and reduced full-edge Jacobian scheme, settles a meaningful local classification and gives a moduli description useful for sparse determinant degenerations. The boundary dimension separation clarifies what remains open. This is not a normalization/parameter renaming or a numerical increment of the path-tridiagonal case: the cycle closure forces all adjacent Pluecker minors and identifies a positive-dimensional Grassmannian moduli space.
